text: Over a spirited round, a small snag around cabin readiness surfaced during routine desk work at Aurelia Skyways. Companion Animal Travel Desk staff were checking a pet booking linked to a calm carrier and noticed the cabin note did not match the latest loading plan. The traveler details were reviewed, the animal space was confirmed as safe, and the handler paused the file before any boarding action moved ahead. A safety coordinator was asked to look at the hazard and check whether the change could affect comfort, ventilation, or escort flow. The review showed no direct risk to the pet, but it did point to a gap in how service changes were being carried from one desk record to the next. Staff then updated the ledger, noted the revised cabin readiness note, and told the travelers what had changed in clear plain words. The handling was kept gentle and humane throughout, with no rushed movement and no stress added to the animal. Follow-up was set so the desk can cross-check cabin notes against the flight plan more carefully on future bookings. This helped close the issue cleanly and supported safer desk practice.
